sections.title: Sandbox, egress proxy, and decoys
sections.summary: Describes the kernel boundary under agent commands: the profile, the backends, the sandbox modes, network choices, the egress proxy, and decoy credential files.
sections.body:
The policy judges a tool call by the paths it names, and a shell can hide a path. The sandbox is the boundary that the kernel enforces under every agent command. The host is read-only. Only the roots of the execution are writable. Ostra data and user credentials are not reachable. The network leads out only through the egress proxy.

## Three layers

The crate keeps each OS difference in one place:

- `Profile` describes the boundary without naming a backend: mounts, environment, egress policy, and decoys.
- A `Backend` renders a profile into a command. `bwrap.rs` (Linux, bubblewrap) and `seatbelt.rs` (macOS, `sandbox-exec`) are plain code that compiles on every OS, so tests check the rendering anywhere.
- `sys` is the only code that calls the kernel. One implementation of the `Os` trait exists for each OS.

On Linux, the sandbox has its own mount, pid, IPC, and network namespaces. The helper `ostra sandbox-init` starts first inside it, binds the loopback ports that lead to Ostra sockets, and loads a seccomp filter.

## What the profile gives

- The host file system is read-only. The repo root, the session dir, and a scratch dir are writable.
- The scratch dir appears at `/tmp` on Linux.
- The home folder is overlaid. Credential stores (`HOME_CREDENTIALS`) and the Ostra data dir are hidden.
- Files that run code in later shells or builds stay read-only, even in a writable folder (`PERSISTENCE_IN_HOME`). Examples: `.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.cargo/bin/`, `.local/bin/`, and `Library/LaunchAgents/`.
- Container sockets are hidden. A process that reaches one can start a container that mounts the host.
- Variables that point to a desktop session, an agent, or a daemon socket are removed (`UNSET_VARS`): `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, `XAUTHORITY`, `DOCKER_HOST`, `GPG_AGENT_INFO`.
- Provider credential variables are removed from the environment of every agent process and MCP server.

## Modes

The setting `[sandbox] mode` has three values. `decide` applies it:

| Mode | Backend exists | Backend missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | Sandboxed. | The execution is refused with an error. |
| `auto` | Sandboxed. | Unsandboxed, with a warning in the status line and the log. |
| `off` | Unsandboxed. | Unsandboxed. |

The default is `required` on Linux and macOS. It is `auto` on Windows, which has no backend yet. A workspace can set its own mode in the registry.

## Network choices

`SandboxNetwork` has four values. Every value but `host` gives each sandbox its own network namespace, so loopback, the LAN, and the host services are out of reach.

| Value | What commands reach |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | Nothing. A harness CLI still reaches its own model API. |
| `allowlist` (default) | The 26 hosts of `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (package registries and source hosts), the model hosts of each harness, and `allowed_hosts`. |
| `public` | Any public address. Loopback, private, and link-local addresses stay refused. |
| `host` | The host network, unfiltered. |

An `allowed_hosts` entry is `host`, `*.domain`, an IPv4 address, or `[v6]`, with an optional `:port`. With no port, it allows 443 and 80. A workspace adds hosts to the global list and cannot remove one.

## The egress proxy

The proxy is the only way out. On Linux, each execution has its own Unix socket, bound only into its sandbox. On macOS, each execution gets its own port on `127.0.0.1`, the only port its Seatbelt policy allows. The proxy sees the host and port of each connection and allows only what the policy allows. It connects to the address that it checked, and never makes a second lookup. This stops DNS rebinding.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `MAX_HEAD` | 8 KiB for the request head |
| `MAX_CONNECTIONS` | 256 |
| `HEAD_TIMEOUT` | 30 seconds |
| `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | 10 seconds |

On macOS all sandboxes share the host loopback. `sandbox_loopback` is `open` (default) or `listed`. `blocked_ports` lists ports that are never reachable. On Linux these two settings change nothing.

## Decoys

A decoy is a credential path that an agent has no reason to read. A read of one is a containment signal. The built-in decoys are `.ssh/id_rsa`, `.ssh/id_ed25519`, `.git-credentials`, and `.vault-token` under the home folder. A workspace adds paths with `sandbox_decoys`. Each entry must start with `~/`, and the limit is `MAX_WORKSPACE_DECOYS` (32).

- **Linux:** a fake file is bound read-only into the sandbox and watched with inotify from outside.
- **macOS:** Seatbelt cannot bind a file in. A decoy is an existing file that the policy refuses to read. The engine reads the refusal from the system log, which only admin accounts can see. A missing file raises no report.

## Containment signals

The engine counts three kinds of signal: a refusal by a protected guard, a refused connection to a loopback, private, or link-local address, and a read of a decoy. A refused public host is not a signal, because builds call telemetry hosts. It shows in the Activity feed only. The third signal of one execution pauses the session.

## Start and end of the server

At start, when no other server runs, Ostra stops processes that earlier sandboxes left running (macOS), removes stale egress sockets, and removes stale decoys. When a session ends, the engine removes its tool cache (`remove_session_cache`). At start, the server also sweeps the caches of ended sessions.

The setup check `ostra_sandbox::status` reports the active backend and the known gaps of the backend under the chosen network.

sections.title: Native tools, MCP gateway, and code navigation
sections.summary: Catalogs the native tools with their limits, and explains the MCP gateway, the lesson memory, and the code index that agents query.
sections.body:
Agents need tools with predictable shapes and limits. `ostra-tools` implements the native tools. Their names and inputs follow Claude Code, because the prompts are tuned to them. The tools check no permission. The policy runs before `execute`.

## Tool catalog

`Capability::native_tool` maps each capability to a tool name. Agents declare capabilities in `agent.toml`.

| Tool | Capability | Limits and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Read` | `read` | 2000 lines by default, 2000 characters per line, 50 MiB per file. |
| `Write`, `Edit` | `write`, `edit` | Exact string replacement for `Edit`. The result carries a diff for the Activity feed. |
| `Bash` | `shell` | Default timeout 120,000 ms, maximum 600,000 ms. Output cut at 30,000 characters. The working directory persists. |
| `Grep` | `search_text` | Ripgrep syntax. Output cut at 30,000 characters. Skips credential folders. |
| `Glob` | `glob` | At most 100 results. |
| `Skill` | `skill` | Loads a `SKILL.md` by name or path. |
| `WebSearch` | `web_search` | A server tool of the provider on native executions. |
| `WebFetch` | `web_fetch` | 5 MiB body, 100,000 characters of text, 10 redirects. Private addresses are blocked unless a rule names the host. |
| `Report` | `report` | Writes the report to the declared `Report file`. |
| `Document` | `document` | Writes the research document, the spec, or the plan as typed JSON. Ostra renders the Markdown. |
| `Memory`, `MemoryRecall` | `memory`, `memory_recall` | Lessons of a project. Recall returns at most 50 lessons. The default is 8. |
| `DocsSearch` | `docs_search` | Search over the documentation books. |
| `CodeOutline`, `CodeFind`, `CodeCallers`, `CodeCallees`, `CodeImplementations`, `CodeNeighbors`, `CodeImpact`, `CodeMap` | `code` | Index queries. See below. |
| `ProjectList`, `ProjectCreate` | `manage_projects` | List projects. Create a project. |
| `SubagentList`, `SubagentAsk`, `SubagentReply` | `coordinate` | See the page Subagent coordination. |
| `submit_<agent>` | always | Ends the execution with structured data. |

On Windows, the PowerShell and `cmd` tools exist beside `Bash`.

## Project creation

`ProjectCreate` makes a new empty project. The input has `key`, `stack`, `purpose`, and `requirements`, and optional `folder` and `git_init`. The purpose has at most `MAX_PURPOSE_CHARS` (800) characters. The call needs 1 to `MAX_REQUIREMENTS` (20) requirements of at most `MAX_REQUIREMENT_CHARS` (400) characters each. The folder is relative to the workspace root with no `..`. The user approves each call. See the page Workspaces, projects, init, and trust approvals.

## Lesson memory

Each project keeps lessons in `<project>/.ostra/memory/knowledge.sqlite3`. A lesson has an `area`, text, and a source. The pair (`area`, `lesson`) is unique. Recall ranks with FTS5 bm25. Lessons are never capped and never expire. Only the `Memory` tool writes the store. The guard `state-ownership` refuses direct writes, because later sessions recall lessons as fact.

## MCP gateway

Workspace settings can list external MCP servers (`mcp_servers`). Ostra is the only MCP client. `McpGateway` in `ostra-server` keeps one connection for each server, signs in, finds tools, and serves them to native executions directly and to harnesses through the `ostra` MCP server. Therefore one policy and one allow list cover every executor.

- **Transports:** stdio and streamable HTTP. OAuth sign-in works for remote servers.
- **Names:** the tool `create_issue` of server `github` is `mcp__github__create_issue` for the policy and the permission rules. It is `github__create_issue` on the `ostra` MCP server. A bare name has at most `MAX_BARE_NAME` (52) characters. A longer or unclean name gets a hash suffix. A server name has at most `MAX_SERVER_NAME` (24) characters. The request timeout has a maximum of `MAX_TIMEOUT_SECS` (600).
- **Limits:** a tool result is cut at `MAX_RESULT` (100 KiB).
- **Redirects:** a redirect is followed only within the origin of the first request, so a secret header never reaches another host.
- **Secrets:** the environment of a stdio server omits provider credentials.
- **Approval:** the programs in `mcp_servers` start only after the user approves the content of `workspace.toml`. See the page Workspaces, projects, init, and trust approvals.

## Code navigation

`ostra-code` serves two users: the Files view of the console and the agents. It has a table-driven tokenizer for about 20 languages, an incremental index of names, definitions, and imports for each project, a dependency graph, and LSP clients. Files over `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (1 MiB) are not indexed.

For each request, the server picks a provider in this order:

1. The `code_provider` program of the project. Ostra runs it once for each request with one JSON request on stdin.
2. The language servers of the project (`language_servers`).
3. The built-in index.

Each external provider has `timeout_secs`. The default is 10 and the maximum is `MAX_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT` (120). After a timeout, Ostra answers with the built-in provider.

The index matches names, not types. It can return a definition that only shares the name. Agents confirm an answer with `Grep` before they change code. A file watcher (`code_watch.rs`) catches edits that Ostra tools did not make.

sections.title: Settings, routing, and project profiles
sections.summary: Explains the settings files and their scopes, the defaults, how the engine resolves the executor, model, and effort for an agent, and the project profile.
sections.body:
Ostra has settings at three scopes. A reader must know which file holds a value and which value wins. This page lists the files, the defaults, and the route resolution.

## Scopes and files

| Scope | Location | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global | `config.toml` at `OSTRA_CONFIG`, or `<config dir>/ostra/config.toml` | Providers, model tiers, harness commands, global permission rules, server, sandbox, `tool_enforcement`. |
| Workspace | `<workspace>/.ostra/workspace.toml` | Name, projects, routing, instructions, limits, notifications, permission rules, sandbox choices, MCP servers. |
| Registry | `registry.db` | The permission mode, the YOLO default, and the sandbox settings of each workspace (Rule A2). A folder file never sets them. |
| Project | `<project>/.ostra/project.toml` and `INVENTORY.md` | The project profile and the inventory. |

Run `ostra config` to print the path of the global file. It writes the default file if none exists. The server reads the global file on every call. A broken file keeps the last good copy, and the server logs a warning. Therefore an edit applies to the next execution with no restart.

## Global config

- `providers`: `anthropic` and `openai`, each with `api_key_env`, `auth_token_env`, `base_url_env`, and `base_url`.
- `tiers`: one table for each executor (`native`, `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `agy`) with four tiers: `fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, `frontier`. A native model is `provider:model`. A harness model is the slug of the CLI.
- `harness`: `command` and `args` for each harness.
- `server`: `port`, `bind` (default `127.0.0.1`), `allowed_hosts`, and `use_ip_host`.
- `sandbox`: see the page Sandbox, egress proxy, and decoys.
- `tool_enforcement`: `disabled` (default) or `enabled`.

## Workspace settings

The struct `WorkspaceSettings` has `#[serde(default)]`. A field that a file lacks takes its value from `WorkspaceSettings::seeded`.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `routing.executor`, `routing.model`, `routing.effort` | seeded | Executor, model, and effort for each agent, and for each phase complexity. |
| `instructions.all`, `instructions.agents` | none | Custom instructions that agents receive. |
| `yolo.default` | off | New sessions start in YOLO mode. |
| `permissions.mode`, `.allow`, `.ask`, `.deny` | `default` | Permission mode and rules. |
| `notifications.push` | on | Push notifications for gates and ended sessions. |
| `limits.max_parallel_executions` | 3 | Executions that run at once. |
| `limits.session_budget_usd` | 25.0 | Dollars before a session pauses. 0 means no limit. |
| `sandbox_mode`, `sandbox_network`, `sandbox_allowed_hosts`, `sandbox_decoys`, `sandbox_loopback`, `sandbox_blocked_ports` | follow global | Workspace sandbox choices. |
| `tool_enforcement` | follow global | Guard strictness. |
| `mcp_servers` | none | External MCP servers. |

`SETTING_KEYS` lists each dotted key with a description for the settings search. A test checks that every key names a field.

## Route resolution

`resolve_route` gives a `ResolvedRoute` with the executor, the model, and the tier:

1. **Executor.** `routing.executor.byPhaseComplexity` wins over `byAgent`. A missing entry means `native`. The judge always runs natively. A harness failure answered with `native` forces the native executor (`executor_override`).
2. **Tier or model.** `routing.model.byPhaseComplexity` wins over `byAgent`. A value is a tier name, `default` (the tier of the agent in `agent.toml`), or a model. The initializer step `generate-skill` forces the tier `advanced` (`tier_override`).
3. **Table.** The tier looks up the model in `tiers.<executor table>`. A missing tier is an error that names the table.
4. **Effort.** `routing.effort` wins over the effort in `agent.toml`.

Only `implementer` and `write-test` route by phase complexity. A phase with no file counts as `Low`.

The seeded routes for a new workspace are:

| Agents | Tier |
| --- | --- |
| `explore`, `generate-spec`, `plan`, `fact-check`, `documentation`, `system-architecture`, `prompt-generation`, `judge`, `advisor` | `advanced` |
| `code-reviewer`, `execution-path-analyzer`, `initializer`, `quick-answer` | `balanced` |
| `implementer`, `write-test` | `fast` for `Low` and `Medium`, `balanced` for `High` |

The default native tiers are `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-opus-5-5`, and `claude-fable-5-1`, all with the prefix `anthropic:`.

A workspace saved before a new agent shipped has no route for it. `keys_without_route` reports each such key as a validation issue, and the value `default` fixes it.

## Validation

`validate_workspace` and the checks in `crates/ostra-workspace/src/settings.rs` return `ValidationIssue` values with a path and a message. Creating a workspace writes nothing while any issue remains (`create.rs`). `ostra_sandbox::validate` checks the sandbox settings.

## Project profile

`.ostra/project.toml` (`ProjectProfile`) holds:

- `stack`, `build_tool`, `test_framework`.
- `commands`: `build`, `test`, `test_one`, `format`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `run`. `{MODULE}`, `{TEST}`, and `{PATH}` are placeholders.
- `test_types`, `module_map`, `skills`, `conventions`, `review_rules`.

The engine and the policy read the profile on each execution, so a saved command applies to the next execution. A rule with `auto_fixable = true` makes its findings eligible for auto-fix.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `OSTRA_CONFIG` | Path of the global config file. |
| `OSTRA_DATA_DIR` | The data dir. |
| `OSTRA_LOG` | Log filter. The default is `info`. |
| `OSTRA_MASTER_KEY_FILE` | A file that holds the master key, for example a Docker secret. |

sections.title: Storage and file layout
sections.summary: Maps every database, table, and folder that Ostra writes, with the rules for migrations, secrets, file modes, and session artifacts.
sections.body:
Ostra keeps state in SQLite files and in folders of artifacts. A change that moves or renames a path breaks readers in other crates. `crates/ostra-core/src/paths.rs` derives every path, so all readers and writers agree. This page maps the storage.

## Data dir

The data dir is `OSTRA_DATA_DIR`, or the local data dir of the user plus `ostra`. Owner-only mode applies (0700 on Unix), because it holds the registry with saved credentials.

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `registry.db` | The machine registry. |
| `server.log` | The server log. |
| `assets/` | Materialized references, skills, and agent prompts. |
| price cache | The models.dev catalog. |

### Registry tables

| Table | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `workspaces` | Workspace id, name, root path (unique), creation time. |
| `push_subscriptions` | Web Push endpoint, keys, and optional workspace. |
| `kv` | Key and blob. It holds sealed secrets (`vapid_private`, provider credentials), sign-in records (`auth:cookie:<sha256>`), and approvals (`trust:workspace:<path>`, `trust:format:<path>`). |

## Workspace folder

The workspace folder holds `<workspace>/.ostra/`:

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace.toml` | Workspace settings. |
| `workspace.db` | The event log and tables for the UI. |
| `sessions/<session id>/` | The session root. |
| `uploads/` | Uploads that wait for a session to claim them. |
| `docs/<book id>/` | Documentation books. |

### Workspace database tables

| Table | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `meta` | Key and value. |
| `projects` | Project key, path, `init_status`, stack. |
| `sessions` | One row for each session: category, status, lane, stage label, projects, YOLO, cost, title. |
| `events` | The log. Primary key `(session_id, seq)`. |
| `executions` | One row for each execution: agent, purpose, executor, model, params, spawn block, status, usage, cost, submit. |
| `messages` | Transcript of native executions, for a resume. |
| `activity` | Streamed deltas of executions. |
| `gates`, `decisions` | Materialized gates and judge decisions. |
| `tool_calls` | Tool name, input, decision, rule, duration, and output. The output is cut at `TOOL_OUTPUT_LIMIT` (8 KiB). |
| `search_docs`, `search_fts` | Full-text search over sessions and artifacts. |

The event log is the source of truth. The other tables are a view that the engine materializes for the UI.

## Session root

| Path in the session root | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `<project key>/` | Per-project reports. |
| `.state/` | Engine-owned state. No agent can write here. |
| `.state/harness/<execution>/` | Hook config, MCP registration, and `terminal.log`. |
| `uploads/` | Files that the user uploaded. |
| `ostra-*.md` and `ostra-*.json` | Artifacts with declared names. |

`paths::report` defines the artifact names so later stages can predict them:

| Name | Writer |
| --- | --- |
| `ostra-implementer-phase-<N>.md` | `implementer` |
| `ostra-implementer-progress-phase-<N>.md` | `implementer` (re-runs read it) |
| `ostra-epa-phase-<N>.md` | `execution-path-analyzer` |
| `ostra-write-test-phase-<N>.md` | `write-test` |
| `ostra-review-ledger-phase-<value>.md` | The reviewer and the work agent |
| `ostra-security-block.json` | `code-reviewer` |
| `ostra-prompt-gen-<n>.md` | `prompt-generation` |
| `ostra-docs-request.md`, `ostra-test-request.md` | The engine, when no implementer ran. |
| `ostra-docs-parts.json` | The engine, for `system-architecture`. |
| `ostra-session-context.md` | The engine. |
| `ostra-completion.md` | The engine, from the `Completion` judge. |

## Project folder

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `.ostra/project.toml`, `.ostra/INVENTORY.md` | Profile and inventory. |
| `.ostra/memory/knowledge.sqlite3` | The lesson store. |
| `.agents/skills/` | Skills. New skills go here. |
| `.ostra/skills/` | Older skills. Ostra reads them and never writes new ones. |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENT.md` | Instruction files, matched in any letter case. |

## Rules for databases

- **Migrations.** `MIGRATIONS` in `workspace.rs` and `registry.rs` is a list of SQL strings. The database stores the count of applied entries in `user_version`. Add a new entry at the end. Do not edit an applied entry, because the engine runs only the entries after `user_version`.
- **Open settings.** SQLite runs in WAL mode with a busy timeout of 5000 ms and foreign keys on.
- **File modes.** Ostra sets 0700 on database folders and 0600 on the database and its `-wal` and `-shm` files, because the event log holds tool output and the registry holds credentials.
- **Parallel executions.** `MemoryStore` opens a new connection for each call, so parallel executions wait on the file lock and share no handle.

## Secrets

The registry seals each secret with AES-256-GCM under the master key. Each value has a fresh nonce, and the row key is associated data. A sealed value cannot move to another row. The master key lives in the OS keychain when one is reachable. Otherwise it lives in an owner-only file. If the key is missing, the registry returns `Locked`. If a value cannot be decrypted, the server logs a warning and the user enters the value again.

sections.title: Workspaces, projects, init, and trust approvals
sections.summary: Explains workspaces and projects, the init flow that bootstraps a project, projects that agents create, and the approvals that stop folder files from starting programs.
sections.body:
A workspace groups projects and holds the sessions that work on them. A project needs an inventory and a profile before agents can route work by them. A folder file can arrive with a repository and name programs to start. This page covers the workspace runtime, the init flow, created projects, and the approvals.

## Workspace runtime

`WorkspaceRt` is one open workspace. It holds the settings, the database, the `Engine`, and the project list. `App::attach` opens each registered workspace at server start and calls `Engine::recover`. A workspace whose `workspace.toml` is missing is skipped with a warning.

Deleting a workspace (`unregister`) removes the registry row, the approvals, `workspace.toml`, and `workspace.db`. Project folders, session folders, and the files in each project `.ostra/` stay.

A request that starts work holds the `work` lock shared. Removing a project or the workspace holds it exclusively, so no work starts between the busy check and the removal.

## Init flow

Init prepares a project: it finds the stack, scouts recurring patterns, proposes skills, and writes the inventory and the profile. An init session has the kind `SessionKind::Init`. The stages are:

1. `Detect`: finds the stack, the slices to scout, and existing skills.
2. `Scout`: one execution for each slice, in parallel, at most `MAX_SCOUTS` (6). It captures real exemplars.
3. `Propose`: merges the findings into a skill proposal. A new recommended skill defaults to `generate`. Other new skills default to `drop`. An existing skill defaults to `reuse`. At most `MAX_DEFAULT_GENERATE` (8) skills default to `generate`.
4. `SkillApproval` gate: the user picks `generate`, `regenerate`, `reuse`, or `drop` for each skill.
5. `GenerateSkill`: one execution for each approved skill, on the tier `advanced`.
6. `GenerateInventory`: writes `INVENTORY.md` and `project.toml`.

Rule I1: when detect finds no slices but finds skills, propose reconciles them and no scout runs. If detect finds neither, the init fails. When the init completes, the engine checks that the inventory and the profile parse. If one is broken, the session fails with `Init did not finish: ... Run init again.`

The `initializer` agent can also run in the mode `adopt` to migrate a bootstrap from Ultracode.

## Created projects

The plan can name a project that does not exist yet. Only the `implementer` of such a phase can create it with `ProjectCreate` (Rule O2). The steps are:

1. The phase runs from its session dir, so the sandbox can write nowhere else until the project exists.
2. `ProjectCreate` asks the user in every mode (Rule O1). YOLO answers it.
3. The engine appends `ProjectCreated` and interrupts the execution (`Interrupt::ProjectCreated`).
4. The planner runs an init for the new project (Rule O4). It holds every other agent in that project until the init ends, because those agents route by the inventory and the profile.
5. The phase starts again inside the new project.
6. The completion report lists each created project and how its init ended (Rule O3).

If an init step leaves no usable result, the `advisor` agent looks at the failed step (Rule O5). It tells the engine to run the step again with guidance, or to ask the user. The engine allows `MAX_ADVICE` (2) advisor rounds for each failed step. A step that the user stopped goes to the user, not to the advisor (Rule P4).

## Trust approvals for folder files

`.ostra/workspace.toml` and `.ostra/project.toml` can arrive with a repository, a `git pull`, or an edit by an agent. The programs that they name must not start without consent (Rule A1). `trust.rs` hashes the content that starts programs or loosens a check:

- the `mcp_servers` entries,
- the projects that have a `code_provider` or `language_servers`,
- the `permissions.allow` list,
- project folders outside the workspace folder.

The SHA-256 hash is stored in the registry under `trust:workspace:<canonical path>`. The format command of a project has its own hash under `trust:format:<path>`. A program starts only when the hash of the file on disk equals the stored hash. A file with nothing of that kind needs no approval.

Saves from the console keep the approval current, so edits in the UI never ask again. An edit outside Ostra changes the hash. The console then shows `Approve the changed commands in settings, because they changed outside Ostra.` The server starts programs from the approved copy of the file, because a second read could see a file that changed after the check.

Secrets in `workspace.toml` are sealed into the registry when the workspace opens (`seal_file_secrets`).

sections.title: Server startup, auth, API, and WebSocket
sections.summary: Describes how the server starts, how a browser signs in, the command line, the REST and WebSocket interface, and how engine notices reach the console.
sections.body:
The server is the only process that a user starts. It must start every workspace, protect itself from foreign web pages, and stream live state to the console. The crate is `ostra-server`, and the binary is `ostra`.

## Startup

`app::run` and `app::build` do these steps:

1. Choose the listen address: the flag `--bind`, else `server.bind`, else `127.0.0.1`.
2. Bind the port: `--port`, else `server.port`, else the first free port from `DEFAULT_PORT` (7878) up to 20 ports, else any free port.
3. If no other server runs, stop leftover sandbox processes, remove stale egress sockets, and remove stale decoys.
4. Validate the global sandbox config. A bad `[sandbox]` stops the start.
5. Report the sandbox status. If no sandbox exists, print a warning to stderr.
6. Start the price cache and unlock the registry with the master key.
7. Write the assets and build the providers, the code tools, the MCP gateway, the native executor, the push notifier, and the harness runtime.
8. On Unix, serve the hook bridge on a Unix socket, so a sandbox with its own network can reach it.
9. Attach each registered workspace, which also recovers its sessions.
10. Print the sign-in URL and serve the router. `Ctrl-C` shuts the server down gracefully.

When the server listens on a non-loopback address, it prints a warning that the traffic uses plain HTTP and that a sign-in link lets anyone run commands as the user.

## Command line

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ostra` or `ostra serve` | Start the server. Flags: `--port`, `--no-open`, `--dev`, `--bind`, `--allow-host`. |
| `ostra url` | Print a fresh sign-in URL for a running server. |
| `ostra sessions` | List the signed-in browsers. |
| `ostra sessions revoke <id>` or `--all` | Revoke one sign-in or all. |
| `ostra signout` | Sign out every browser. |
| `ostra stop <session>` | Stop a session when the server is off. |
| `ostra config` | Print the config path and write the default config if none exists. |
| `ostra hook`, `ostra mcp-stdio` | Harness callbacks. Harnesses call them, not users. |
| `ostra sandbox-init` | Hidden. The helper that starts first inside a Linux sandbox. |

## Browser auth

1. The server prints a URL with a one-time token in the fragment. The token lives `TOKEN_TTL_SECS` (15 minutes).
2. The browser posts the token to `/api/auth/exchange`. The server returns the cookie `ostra_session` (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`).
3. A sign-in lasts `COOKIE_TTL_SECS` (30 days).

The registry stores tokens and cookies hashed, so a restart keeps sign-ins and `ostra url` can mint a token for a running server. Host and Origin checks block DNS rebinding and foreign pages. An address that fails an exchange 5 times (`MAX_FAILURES`) in 60 seconds must wait. A loopback server answers at a private `ostra-....localhost` name by default, because a cookie for `127.0.0.1` reaches every local port. The setting `server.use_ip_host` turns this off for a browser that does not resolve `*.localhost`.

A revoke from the server takes effect at once. A revoke from the CLI takes effect within `RECHECK` (5 seconds).

## REST API

`api::router` defines the routes. The main groups are:

| Group | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Server and auth | `/api/info`, `/api/auth/exchange`, `/api/auth/sessions`, `/api/auth/signout`, `/api/environment`, `/api/onboarding` |
| Workspaces and projects | `/api/workspaces/{ws}/validate`, `/projects`, `/clone`, `/settings/fix`, `/approve`, `/skills`, `/tree`, `/search`, `/activity`, `/cost` |
| Sessions | `/api/sessions/{id}`, `/events`, `/yolo`, `/amend`, `/pause`, `/resume`, `/stop`, `/diff` |
| Gates and decisions | `/api/gates/{id}/answer`, `/api/decisions/{id}/override` |
| Executions | `/api/executions/{id}`, `/activity`, `/cancel`, `/resume`, `/inspect` |
| Artifacts and books | `/api/artifacts`, `/api/artifacts/download`, `/api/workspaces/{ws}/docs` |
| MCP | `/api/workspaces/{ws}/mcp` and its `refresh`, `login`, and `logout` routes |
| Push and files | `/api/push/subscribe`, `/api/fs`, `/api/fs/list`, `/api/fs/mkdir` |
| Harness setup | `/api/harnesses/{harness}/setup` |
| Quick answers | `/api/workspaces/{ws}/ask` |

The harness callbacks use `/internal/policy` and `/internal/mcp`. Each call carries the per-execution bearer token.

## WebSocket

One socket serves one browser tab at `/ws`. The client sends `ClientMsg` values, for example `Subscribe {channel}` and `Unsubscribe {channel}`. The channels are `session:<id>`, `execution:<id>`, `workspace:<id>`, `home`, and `term:<id>`.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Largest client message | 1 MiB |
| Largest `term_input` | 64 KiB |
| Channels for one connection | 256 |
| Binary frames queued for one socket | 64 |

A binary frame holds the byte length of the execution id, the id, and the PTY bytes. A slow socket lags and gets a fresh screen. A repeated subscribe to `term:<id>` restarts the stream and resends the screen. The socket checks its sign-in every 5 seconds, so an expired cookie or a revoke closes it.

## From the engine to the console

The engine broadcasts `EngineNotice` values on a channel of 4096 messages. `App::attach` forwards each notice to the file and navigation observers and to the hub (8192 messages). `ws::route` maps each notice to channels and to a `ServerMsg`. If a receiver lags, the server logs it and asks the navigation tree to reload.

## Push notifications

`ServerServices::notify` sends a push message only when `notifications.push` is on. The payload has a title, a body, a link, and a tag. Messages with one tag replace each other. A subscription that answers 404 or 410 is removed. The encrypted body has at most `MAX_PLAINTEXT` (3993) bytes. Push needs HTTPS or localhost.

## Other modules

`repo.rs` runs the git commands of the Git dock. A command that changes the checkout waits for sessions that work in the project. `files/` serves trees, reads, diffs, and write tracking. `nav/` builds the sessions tree and the search. `skills.rs` manages the skills of each project. `commands.rs` edits the commands of `project.toml`. `harness_setup.rs` runs the installer or login of a harness in a PTY that the browser streams.

sections.title: Web console
sections.summary: Describes the React console: its layers, how it talks to the server, the generated types, the screens, and the invariants that tie it to the Rust code.
sections.body:
The console is the only user interface. It must show live sessions, ask gates, and stay in step with Rust types. The code is in `web/` (React, TypeScript, Vite). The design system is in `design/` and loads as `@ostra/design`.

## Layers

| Folder | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `web/src/api/` | The `api` object (REST), the `socket` manager (WebSocket), and mock fixtures. |
| `web/src/api/gen/` | TypeScript types that ts-rs writes from Rust types with `#[ts(export)]`. |
| `web/src/lib/` | Hooks, live data stores, navigation, shortcuts, and formatting. |
| `web/src/shell/` | The chrome: sidebar, tabs, title bar, palette, Files and Git panels. |
| `web/src/screens/` | One screen for each resource id. `README.md` lists the props and URLs. |
| `web/src/features/` | Gate cards, context tags and uploads, and book rendering. |

## Screens

| Screen | Resource id | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WorkspaceScreen` | `ws:overview` | New task form and sessions table. |
| `SessionScreen` | `session:<id>` | Session board with gates. |
| `ExecutionScreen` | `exec:<id>` | Usage strip, then the Activity feed or a terminal by `ExecutionView.stream`. |
| `ArtifactScreen` | `artifact:<path>` | Spec, plan, report, or ledger. |
| `SettingsScreen` | `ws:settings` | Workspace settings forms. |
| `CostScreen`, `MemoryScreen`, `SkillsScreen` | `ws:cost`, `ws:memory`, `ws:skills` | Spend, lessons, skills. |
| `DocsScreen`, `BookScreen` | `ws:docs`, `book:<id>` | Books, with search, contents, and HTML export. |
| `ProjectScreen`, `FileScreen` | `project:<key>`, `file:<key>:<path>` | Project overview, dependencies, files, and diffs. |

## Talking to the server

`web/src/api/index.ts` exports `api`. It is `httpApi` by default. When `VITE_MOCK=1`, it is the mock API with fixtures. The fixtures load through a dynamic import, so they stay out of the production bundle.

`socket.ts` manages the WebSocket. It decodes binary PTY frames, routes each `ServerMsg` to its channels (`channelsFor`), and answers code hint requests. A hint that the server does not answer within 30 seconds resolves to null.

The shell shares live data for each workspace: one fetch and one socket subscription for each kind (`lib/live.ts`).

## Invariants

- Do not edit a file in `web/src/api/gen/`. Change the Rust type, and ts-rs writes the file again. `.cargo/config.toml` sets the output folder.
- `Question::display_options` in Rust and `orderedOptions` in `web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts` must number options the same way, because a typed answer names options by number.
- Heavy components load with `lazy()`: the Monaco diff, the file editor, and xterm. Import them only through their lazy wrappers, so they stay out of the main chunk.
- Agent and repository text is untrusted. The browser security suite checks that no render path runs it.

## Build and development

| Command (run in `web/`) | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Vite dev server. Start the server with `--dev` so it accepts the dev host. |
| `npm run dev:mock` | Dev server with fixtures and no backend. |
| `npm run build` | Build `web/dist`. |
| `npm test` | Run the Vitest tests. |
| `npm run typecheck` | Type-check with `tsc`. |
| `npm run check` | Lint and format check with Biome. |

The server embeds `web/dist` (`assets.rs`). An unknown path falls back to `index.html` so client routes load directly. `/sw.js` is served from the root so the service worker covers the app.

sections.title: Testing layers and eval suites
sections.summary: Lists each test layer, what it proves, and the commands, including the paid live evals that stay off by default.
sections.body:
A change to the planner, the policy, or a judge can break behavior with no compile error. Each test layer catches a different class of break. This page lists the layers, what each proves, and how to run it.

## Commands

- Run every Rust test: `cargo test --workspace`.
- Run one crate: `cargo test -p ostra-engine`.
- Run one test file: `cargo test -p ostra-server --test e2e`.
- Format: `cargo fmt --all`.

The standalone crate `tests/windows-probes` is outside the workspace. It is a probe program for a throwaway Windows VM.

## Layers

| Layer | Location | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit tests | `#[cfg(test)]` modules in each crate | Local behavior: parsing, rendering, matching. |
| Planner conformance | `tests/conformance/main.rs` (a test of `ostra-engine`) | One fixture for each rule ID. It builds an event history, folds it, and checks the next steps. |
| Engine tests | `crates/ostra-engine/tests/` (`runner.rs`, `pause.rs`, `recover.rs`) | The runner with fakes: pause and resume, and recovery after a restart. |
| Store tests | `crates/ostra-store/tests/workspace_db.rs` | Migrations and queries. |
| Sandbox tests | `crates/ostra-sandbox/src/tests.rs`, `tests/env_scrub.rs` | Profile rendering and environment scrubbing. |
| Whole stack | `crates/ostra-server/tests/e2e.rs` | A real listener, REST with cookie auth, the engine, the native loop, the policy, the tools, and git staging. A scripted model plays each agent. |
| MCP | `crates/ostra-server/tests/mcp.rs` | The MCP gateway. |
| Console | `web/src/**/*.test.ts(x)` and `design/src/*.test.tsx` | Components and libraries, with Vitest. |
| Browser security | `tests/browser/` | A real Chromium against a scratch server and a fake model. |

The `test-prices` feature of `ostra-core` gives fixed model prices to the tests of the native executor, the providers, and the harness crate.

## Browser security suite

Run `cd tests/browser && npm test`. The run builds the web UI and a debug binary, starts a scratch server under `/tmp/pw-browser` with its own config, data dir, master key, and `HOME`, and stops it at the end. Nothing leaves the machine. The model API is a local fake, the harness is a stub script, and the MCP server is a stub. Each test string sets `window.__pwned` or requests a canary URL if it runs, so the guard fixture fails a test on either.

## Live evals

The eval suites call real models and cost money. They are ignored by default.

| Suite | File | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Judges | `crates/ostra-server/tests/judge_evals.rs` | `tests/evals/judges.toml` |
| Coordination | `crates/ostra-server/tests/coordination_evals.rs` | `tests/evals/coordination.toml` |
| Advisor | `crates/ostra-server/tests/advisor_evals.rs` | `tests/evals/advisor.toml` |
| Test stage | `crates/ostra-server/tests/test_stage_evals.rs` | `tests/evals/test_stage.toml` |

Run the test stage evals with:

```text
OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS=anthropic:claude-opus-5-5,anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5 OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS=3 \
  cargo test -p ostra-server --test test_stage_evals -- --ignored --nocapture
```

`OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS` lists the models, `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` sets the runs for each case, and `OSTRA_EVAL_GRADER` names the grader model (the default is Opus). Set an API key for each provider first.

A judge eval case holds a request about the source of Ostra and the route that a careful engineer picks. Add a case to `tests/evals/judges.toml` when you change a judge prompt.

## Rules for a change

- Add a conformance fixture for each new planner rule, because the planner has no other test that checks the order of steps.
- Run the live evals when you change a judge or agent prompt. A prompt change gives no compile error and no failed unit test.
- Do not call a real provider from a default test. Use `ScriptedProvider`.

sections.title: Change recipes
sections.summary: Gives the steps for the common changes: a setting, an agent, a gate kind, a judge, an event, an API route, a migration, and a tool.
sections.body:
Each recipe lists the files to change in order. The compiler finds most missed places, because the code uses exhaustive matches. The recipes name the places that the compiler cannot find.

## Add a workspace setting

1. Add the field to `WorkspaceSettings` in `crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs`. The struct has `#[serde(default)]`, so old `workspace.toml` files take the value from `WorkspaceSettings::seeded`.
2. Add its dotted key and a description to `SETTING_KEYS`. A test checks that each key names a field.
3. Set the seeded value in `WorkspaceSettings::seeded`.
4. Add validation in `validate_workspace` or in `crates/ostra-workspace/src/settings.rs`.
5. Read the value through `Services::workspace()` where it applies. The server reads it again on each execution.
6. Add the field to `web/src/screens/workspace/settingsForm.ts`.
7. Run `cargo test --workspace`. Commit the changed files in `web/src/api/gen`.

If the setting starts a program or loosens a check, add it to the hash in `crates/ostra-workspace/src/trust.rs`. A setting that starts a program without approval lets a repository run code.

## Add an agent

1. Add a variant to `AgentName` in `crates/ostra-core/src/agent.rs`. Update `ALL` (the array length), `as_str`, and `is_session_only`.
2. Create `assets/agents/<name>/agent.toml` and `prompt.md`. `load_defs` reads a file for every name in `ALL`, so a missing file panics at first use.
3. Add a route to `WorkspaceSettings::seeded`.
4. Define the submit type and its schema in `crates/ostra-core/src/submit.rs` (`submit_schema`).
5. Define the spawn params in `crates/ostra-agents/src/spawn.rs` and the case in `crates/ostra-engine/src/factory.rs`.
6. Add an `ExecPurpose` variant, its `stage_of` mapping, and the planner step in `crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs`. Handle the finish in `SessionState::apply`.
7. Add a capability and its tool names to `assets/tool-mapping.toml` if the agent needs a new capability.
8. Add a conformance fixture.

## Add a gate kind

1. Add a variant to `GatePayload` in `crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs`. Update `stage`, `kind_str`, and `execution`.
2. Add a `GateAnswer` variant if the answer has a new shape. Update `validate_answer` in `runner.rs`.
3. Update `gate_owner` in `plan.rs`, because `Step::key` uses it to dedupe the gate.
4. Update `yolo_plan` in `judge_input.rs`. Choose a fixed answer, a judge answer, or no answer.
5. Open the gate in the planner and handle `GateAnswered` in the fold.
6. Add a card in `web/src/features/gates/`.

## Add a judge

1. Add a variant to `JudgeKind` and to `as_str` in `event.rs`.
2. Write `assets/judges/<as_str>.md`. The file name must match.
3. Define the output type and its schema in `crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs` (`output_schema`).
4. Build the input in `judge_input.rs`.
5. Add the validation arm in `perform_judge`.
6. Return the `Step::Judge` from the planner and fold the `DecisionMade` event.
7. If the user can override the decision, add the kind to `Engine::override_decision`.
8. Add eval cases to `tests/evals/judges.toml`.

## Add an event or a field

1. Add the `SessionEvent` variant in `event.rs`.
2. Give each new field of an existing event `#[serde(default)]`. Old logs must still parse.
3. Handle the event in `SessionState::apply`. Keep the fold free of clock, disk, and environment reads.
4. Update `Inner::materialize` if a table for the UI needs the event.
5. Do not rename a serialized name without `#[serde(alias)]`.

## Add an API route

1. Write the handler in `crates/ostra-server/src/api.rs` and add the route in `router`.
2. Put request and response types in `crates/ostra-core/src/api.rs` with `#[ts(export)]`.
3. Add the client method in `web/src/api/client.ts` and the mock in `web/src/api/mock/`.
4. Add a case to `crates/ostra-server/tests/e2e.rs`.

## Add a database migration

1. Append one SQL string to `MIGRATIONS` in `crates/ostra-store/src/workspace.rs` or `registry.rs`.
2. Do not edit an earlier entry. A database that applied it does not run it again.
3. Add a test to `crates/ostra-store/tests/workspace_db.rs`.

## Add a native tool

1. Define the tool and its schema in `crates/ostra-tools/src/defs.rs` and implement it in a tool module.
2. Add a capability or reuse one in `Capability` (`agent.rs`), and add the names to `assets/tool-mapping.toml`.
3. Add the name to `KNOWN_TOOLS` in `crates/ostra-policy/src/perms.rs`, so rules can name it.
4. Decide its policy: the family in `perms::family` and any guard in `guards.rs`.
5. For a harness, serve the tool from the MCP shim in `crates/ostra-exec-harness/src/bridge.rs`.
6. If the tool is read-only, add it to `is_concurrent` in `crates/ostra-exec-native/src/lib.rs`.

glossary.definition: The agent that reads a failed init step and tells the engine how to continue.
A model with a fixed role, tools, and a submit tool. The code lists 14 agents in `AgentName`.
A set of documentation parts, an optional architecture, and a glossary, stored under `.ostra/docs/`.
The type of a request, such as `IMPLEMENT` or `DOCS`. The category selects the flow.
An event that looks like an attempt to leave the sandbox. Three signals from one execution pause the session.
The stored result of a judge call, with its reason, as a `DecisionMade` event.
A fake credential file whose read is a containment signal.
The proxy that is the only network path out of a sandbox. It applies the host allow list.
Execution-path analysis: the report of the `execution-path-analyzer` agent that lists the checks for `write-test`.
The append-only list of `SessionEvent` values of a session in the `events` table.
One run of one agent, with a route, a spawn block, a status, and a recorded usage.
The code that runs one execution. It is native or one of four harnesses.
The deterministic function `SessionState::fold` that builds the session state from the ordered events.
A record that stops the pipeline until the user, or YOLO, gives an answer.
A layer 1 policy check that nothing overrides.
A request from an agent for a specialist, today always `prompt-generation`.
An installed agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, or Antigravity) that Ostra runs under a PTY.
The path that carries each harness hook event to the policy engine through `ostra hook` and `/internal/policy`.
The file `.ostra/INVENTORY.md` that maps module paths to areas of a project.
A single model call that returns JSON against a schema and makes one orchestration decision.
A column of the session board. Each stage kind belongs to one lane.
A durable note in the project memory that later executions recall.
The `ostra mcp-stdio` process that serves the Ostra tools to a harness over the MCP protocol.
The executor that runs the model loop itself on an API key.
The list of sections for one project in a book, written by the `documentation` agent.
One of `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, or `bypass`. It sets what layer 2 does when no rule matches.
One unit of implement work from the plan, or one inline unit when the plan is skipped.
The pure function `next_steps` that reads the session state and returns the next steps.
A code folder in a workspace with a key, an inventory, and a profile.
The file `.ostra/project.toml` with commands, test types, skills, and review rules.
A short text of project facts that Ostra appends to the first message of each execution.
The path after an agent reports `stuck`: research, a rerun with a fact, or a gate.
The file `ostra-review-ledger-phase-<value>.md` where agents record `FIXED` or `WONTFIX` for each finding.
The executor, model, and tier that settings select for an agent.
The `Engine` code that performs steps, appends events, and starts executions.
The kernel boundary under agent commands: bubblewrap on Linux and Seatbelt on macOS.
One run of the pipeline for one user request, stored as a log of events.
The folder where an agent writes its reports: the session root or its per-project subfolder.
A `SKILL.md` file that gives instructions for one kind of task, stored under `.agents/skills/`.
A permit to run one execution. The workspace limit is `limits.max_parallel_executions`.
The `Label: value` text at the start of the first message of an agent.
One node kind of the pipeline, for example `Spec` or `Review`. `StageKind` lists them.
One action that the planner returns for the runner to perform, for example a spawn or a gate.
One conversation of an agent. Its ID is the id of its first execution.
The `submit_<agent>` tool that ends an execution with structured data.
A model class: `fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, or `frontier`. Tables map tiers to models.
The depth of an `IMPLEMENT` request: `light` skips the spec and plan, and `full` runs them.
The stored hash of approved folder-file content. Programs start only when the file hash matches.
A work agent paired with the `code-reviewer` agent, repeated until no HIGH or MEDIUM finding remains.
A folder with `.ostra/workspace.toml` that groups projects and holds sessions.
A per-session mode in which the engine answers gates and permission asks without the user.
